messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: measurementInvarianceCat()?
parts:
On 05/11/2015 04:18 PM, ya wrote:
> Dear list,
>
> I am playing with the measurementInvarianceCat() in semTools package

You need to downgrade to lavaan 0.5-17. The current version of lavaan
(0.5-18) does not work with a few functions (including
measurementInvarianceCat) of the semTools package. An update of semTools
will fix this.

But having said this, I would urge you to first do the invariance steps
manually. A very nice description (including lavaan syntax) is given here:

http://www.myweb.ttu.edu/spornpra/catInvariance.html


Yves.

Dear list,

I have a follow up question when I compare output between configural and weak invariance model from lavaan and semTools. Could you give me some advice please? Thank you very much.

I found that the chi square for the weak invariance model in lavaan is smaller than that for the configural invariance model, which should not be. The df are fine in configural, weak, and strong invariance model using lavaan, semTools, and Mplus. I have compared the parameter estimates between configural and weak invariance model from lavaan output, the only difference I can locate is in the factor loadings part, that they were not equal in the configural invariance model but were constrained to be equal across groups in the weak invariance model. parts:
Dear list,

One more question:

Has anyone tried the strict invariance model? My strong invariance model and strict invariance model produced exactly the same output. The residual variance of the indicators were not constrained to be equal across groups although the group.equal=c("loadings","thresholds","residuals") was included in the code. Please find the code for the strong and the strict invariance model below:

mod="
#measurement model
bul1=~bul1_1+bul2_1+bul3_1+bul4_1+bul5_1+bul6_1
bul2=~bul1_2+bul2_2+bul3_2+bul4_2+bul5_2+bul6_2
bul3=~bul1_3+bul2_3+bul3_3+bul4_3+bul5_3+bul6_3
"
fitstronginvar=sem(mod,data=grades1to9,missing="pairwise",group="Boy",group.equal=c("loadings","thresholds"),
ordered=c("bul1_1","bul2_1","bul3_1","bul4_1","bul5_1","bul6_1",
"bul1_2","bul2_2","bul3_2","bul4_2","bul5_2","bul6_2",
"bul1_3","bul2_3","bul3_3","bul4_3","bul5_3","bul6_3")

)
summary(fitstronginvar,fit.measures=T,standardized=T)

fitstrictinvar=sem(mod,data=grades1to9,missing="pairwise",group="Boy",group.equal=c("loadings","thresholds","residuals"),
ordered=c("bul1_1","bul2_1","bul3_1","bul4_1","bul5_1","bul6_1",
"bul1_2","bul2_2","bul3_2","bul4_2","bul5_2","bul6_2",
"bul1_3","bul2_3","bul3_3","bul4_3","bul5_3","bul6_3")

)
summary(fitstrictinvar,fit.measures=T,standardized=T)


Please give me some suggestions. Thank you very much.

Best regards,

ya

messages.subject: Re: measurementInvarianceCat()?
parts:
On 05/15/2015 12:37 PM, ya wrote:
> I found that the chi square for the weak invariance model in lavaan is
> smaller than that for the configural invariance model, which should not
> be.

The *robust* (=scaled) chi-square test statistic is indeed smaller in
the weak invariance model, but the original/unscaled test statistic is
larger:

configural: original = 2443, scaled = 3153
weak: original = 2576, scaled = 2668

That is because the correction is (partly) model-based, and therefore
may change from model to model. So this can happen.

However, this does NOT affect the scaled difference test, which starts
from the original test statistics.

Yves.

parameter in the model. To test for strict invariance in the categorical
setting, you need parameterization="theta".

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: measurementInvarianceCat()?
parts:
On 05/19/2015 11:53 AM, ya wrote:
> Dear Yves，
>
> Now I have the code like this:
>
> fitstrictinvar=sem(mod,data=grades1to9,missing="pairwise",group="Boy",group.equal=c("loadings","thresholds"),parameterization="theta",
> + ordered=c("bul1_1","bul2_1","bul3_1","bul4_1","bul5_1","bul6_1",
> + "bul1_2","bul2_2","bul3_2","bul4_2","bul5_2","bul6_2",
> + "bul1_3","bul2_3","bul3_3","bul4_3","bul5_3","bul6_3")
> + )
>
> although the residual variance in the second group is freely estimated
> now, they were not constrained to be equal across groups.

But you have just fitted the strong invariance model. The "residuals"
are not included in group.equal=, so the residuals will be freely
estimated in the second group.


To fit the strict invariance model, you need to set the theta
parameterizationm, and add "residuals" to the group.equal= argument.
Then, the residuals will be constrained to be equal across groups. But
they will all take on the value of the first/reference group, and this
is 1.0!

Yves.
